study_identification_part.si_4_title: Effects of anterior temporal lobe resection on cortical morphology

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used 924 healthy controls for the normative model: 833 from the NKI (Nathan Kline Institute) dataset and 91 from a single site (National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery/Chalfont Centre for Epilepsy). The 101 TLE patients were from the single site (NHNN/Chalfont).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We also used MR images of cross-sectional cohorts of 924 healthy controls, 91 of which were taken together with patients. Specifically, 22 were taken with scanning protocol 1 and 69 with scanning protocol 2 at the NHNN. The remaining 833 controls are subjects from the Nathan Kline Institute (NKI) data set (Nooner et al., 2012)."

answer.SINGLE-SITE (NHNN): normative model training (healthy controls) and clinical application (TLE patients)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: NKI dataset (833 controls) was used together with site-specific controls (91 from NHNN) for normative model training to correct for age, sex, and scanning protocol effects. The 101 TLE patients from NHNN were the clinical application cohort whose pre- and post-surgical morphology was analyzed.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "A normative model trained on data from 924 healthy controls was used to debias the data and account for healthy ageing effects occurring scans." ... "We used the controls to provide a normative model of age and sex with scanning protocol as a random effect. Even though the large NKI data set did not match the patients in scanning protocol, we used them for training to ensure we had robust models for the entire age range, given that the site-specific control data sets were relatively small"
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Leiberg2023.pdf.md: Abstract (L41) and 2.5. Age, sex and scanning protocol correction (L151)

model-1.model-name: GAMM normative model for cortical morphology

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The study used 924 healthy controls for the normative model (833 from NKI + 91 from NHNN). All 924 controls were used for training the GAMM normative model. There was no separate validation/test split mentioned for the normative model itself; the model was applied to correct the TLE patient data.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "We also used MR images of cross-sectional cohorts of 924 healthy controls" ... "We used the controls to provide a normative model of age and sex with scanning protocol as a random effect."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Leiberg2023.pdf.md: 2.2. Data & preprocessing (L103) and 2.5. Age, sex and scanning protocol correction (L141-L151)

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The paper does not report age statistics for the healthy control cohort used in the normative model. Table 1 only shows demographics for TLE patients (Left TLE, Right TLE) and the total number of controls (924), but no age information is provided for controls. The paper mentions that subjects in the TLE study were in an age range of 19-60 years, but this refers to patients, not controls.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Table 1 – Demographics of individuals with TLE and controls." (Table shows only n=924 for controls, with sex 362/562 M/F, but no age statistics) ... "although as subjects in our study were in an age range of 19–60 years" (referring to TLE patients)

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: From Table 1, controls had 362 males and 562 females out of 924 total. Female percentage: 562/924 = 60.8%. Male percentage: 362/924 = 39.2%. Since all 924 controls were used for training, overall-phase and train-phase are identical.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Table 1 – Demographics of individuals with TLE and controls. ... Controls ... Subjects (n) 924 ... Sex (M/F) 362/562"
